title: Greatswords (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Greatswords (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - weapon - overview 
 overview : Greatswords continue the natural evolution process from Daggers to Straight Swords, by sacrificing speed for additional attack power. Each strike with these weapons has the wielders full weight behind them to maximize the damage they do. Because so much force and effort is required with each swing, the speed of the strikes is much slower than with smaller weapons, which means they are not very effective for attempting critical hits with.

These weapons are designed simply to overpower foes, and even though the strikes may be slow, the hits are so powerful that they often still stagger foes long enough to land additional hits. The size of the weapons, and large arc of their swing, also means that they are very good for crowd control, or for tracking evasive opponents.

The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

While the **Assassin** doesn't have any ranged attack, its Spook Sorcery is extremely useful for removing most non-fatal fall damage and for completely silencing footsteps for 20 seconds, allowing certain obstacles to be bypassed . Unfortunately, while the starting Sorcerer's Staff is a fairly good spell tool, if not exactly the best, it won't actually start to gain scaling from stats until Intelligence has reached at least 19, delaying a possible strengthening of the character's Sorceries.

Picking up the Soul Arrow Sorcery from the Shrine Handmaid gives a reusable ranged attack early on, while the weapon buffing Magic Weapon Sorcery can be gained in either Undead Settlement or Road of Sacrifices to add some of a Staff's spellbuff to weapon damage.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Assassin** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Dexterity-based class with decent Attunement for Weapon Arts and spells and some Intelligence for Sorceries.

An unusually long Thrusting Sword, the Estoc is also quite strong and has a rare sweeping heavy attack for hitting several or agile foes easier, at the cost of not having an increased critical modifier for Ripostes and Backstabs. Additionally, its Weapon Art, Shield Splitter, helps with its bad damage to the stamina of blocking targets by partially bypassing the defences of the block instead.

Its Targeting Shield, while not very suitable for blocking, is one of the game's three parrying shields and as such its Parry starts slightly earlier yet ends as late as the regular parry.

The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bandit (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bandit** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It has high Dexterity and well above average Faith, meaning it lends itself rather well towards builds focused either on both or only the former (though it will have strong competition from the Swordsman when it comes to pure Dexterity builds). It is rather unsuitable to spells, even the Miracle ones, due to its extremely low Attunement and Intelligence.

Bandits are actually unable to speak to Straid of Olaphis by default, the only class that can't do that, due to its extremely low Intelligence not meeting his minimum required amount of 3.

 characteristics : The Claymore is a utilitarian greatsword with a versatile moveset, good reach, fast swing-speed, and solid damage per hit. It has relatively low strength and dexterity requirements, making it a viable option for infusions, while the C/C scaling makes it a powerful weapon for dedicated quality builds. These traits lets it fill a similar role to the Bastard Sword which performs similarly, but sacrifices the thrusting attack and some damage for lower weight and slightly lower requirements.

The main drawback of the Claymore is that many greatswords found later in the game outclass it in terms of damage. With that said, the Claymore remains a dependable weapon throughout the game, and its relatively low requirements makes it an attractive choice if one does not want to invest stats into using the more powerful elemental greatswords.

 characteristics : Like in the previous games, the Claymore is a reliable and versatile weapon with great damage output. It's balanced scaling between Strength and Dexterity makes it a great candidate for Refined infusion, and it can be buffed with spells and items. This, coupled with its adaptable moveset and early accessibility, makes the Claymore a promising weapon for any melee build.

The Claymore is also one of the longest Greatswords in the game, giving it a better reach than most swords of its class. This allows certain character builds to perform multiple attacks and roll away with near-impunity, particularly during boss fights. Its Weapon Arts is particularly effective against enemies with weapons no longer than a Spear as it makes full use of the sword's length. As with its previous incarnations, the Claymore remains exceptional at stun-locking enemies with low poise.

Cleric (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Cleric** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Faith-focused class, with decent Attunement, Strength, and Luck. This makes them well-suited to a Miracle-heavy build, and to using the many Lightning-attuned weapons as they are often also have good Strength-scaling.

While it does indeed have spells, in the form of Heal (which heals) and Force (which throws enemies away from you), it does not have any that causes damage, with the earliest ones not being found until Cathedral of the Deep or Farron Keep. This means the class will have to focus primarily on weapons initially, and will do well to keep them upgraded as offensive Miracles consume a lot of Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Cleric (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This is the only spellcasting-focused starting class in Dark Souls 3 that doesn't have a damage-boosting ring. Presumably this is because the Cleric doesn't have a damaging Miracle equipped from the start, and the Morne's Ring can instead be found in the Road of Sacrifices.
This class has remained remarkably similar throughout the series, always carrying a Mace and the Heal Miracle.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet: The Cleric's Sacred Chime is a fairly good casting tool and is actually the strongest casting tool for Miracles from 45 to 49 Faith. Its Spell Buff (the stat that affects how strong scaling spells are) doesn't actually increase until at least 19 Faith has been reached. Its Weapon Art is Gentle Prayer, a regenerative effect that always restores 360 hp over the course of a minute as long as the Chime is held in an active hand (so replacing it with another item stops it, as does two-handing the item in the other hand). This effect will actually outheal the Heal Miracle by up to 20% until the Chime's Spell Buff reaches 120, and even afterwards it is a strong if slow alternative due to only having about a third the cost in Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Cleric Set is a light, caster-type armor set and as such has low physical defences and high elemental defences, while also having high Poison and Curse resistances.

The first trainer for more Miracles is found in the Undead Settlement for further development.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Mace is an unexpectedly strong weapon for what may at first seem like a spellcasting class, but in reality it is often a **Cleric's** main armament. This is because Strike damage is often the strongest physical damage type as armored and skeletal enemies are weak to it (most other physical damage types have fewer enemies weak to them), strong Strength-scaling for easy damage increases, a fairly good moveset, and has a good Weapon Art for trading hits with opponents. How the Weapon Art works is that Perseverance adds a flat 45% extra absorption and causes the attacks of light weapons to bounce off the user, while also granting great Hyper Armor to prevent being staggered.

The Blue Wooden Shield is not very good, having only decent physical and magic defence with serviceable Stability. While it does have Parry (albeit the inferior Medium Shield version), a strong Weapon Skill shield like the early Silver Eagle Kite Shield would probably serve as a better replacement.

Crossbows are a ranged weapon that have rather low Strength and Dexterity requirements and offer no scaling, making them ideal for builds that do not invest heavily into physical stats. Unlike bows and greatbows, crossbows can be held and fired in one hand, but require the player to reload between shots as indicated by an arrow head in the top portion of the weapon icon. This makes them ideal ranged weapons for engaging foes within lock-on range.

title: Crossbows (Dark Souls III)
snippet: Crossbows can be equipped in either the main hand or off hand. title: Dexterity (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Dexterity (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Raising one's Dexterity value primarily increases their Dexterity Attack Bonus, the value of which is multiplied by a hidden modifier of a weapon when attacking. Raising Dexterity also boosts the player's HP and Physical Defense stat, as well as one's Poison and Bleed Bonuses slightly.

For the few weapons that do scale, the softcaps for Dexterity are **20/40/50** for the purposes of increasing physical attack. Since a majority of weapons do not scale well, it is not worth it to get to the physical damage scaling softcaps or go beyond the minimum stats to wield in these cases.

snippet:
Dexterity (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - soft_caps 
 soft_caps : As of the 1.32 Regulations patch, Dexterity has two soft caps: 40 and 80.

For most normal builds, the damage return for weapon attack rating stops at 40 Dexterity. This applies to both quality builds and Dexterity-focused builds.

When utilizing the Sharp infusion, scaling on weapons changes at high levels. Attack rating returns between 40 and 60 Dexterity are relatively poor, with most weapons only seeing an increase in 1 point of damage per level of investment. But past 60 Dexterity, scaling increases again, seeing gains of 3 to 5 damage per level up until roughly 80 Dexterity, where it will gradually fall off.

Dexterity increases damage done by weapons with a scaling mechanic. A letter denoting a weapon's specific scaling properties is noted beneath the weapon's required Dexterity stat. The letters range in order of effectiveness from **E**, **D**, **C**, **B**, **A**, and **S**.

Weapons with an **E** rating for scaling will receive a poor benefit from investment in Dexterity while weapons with an **S** rating receive the greatest benefit.

As is with every other stat in the game, it also has indirect bonuses such as increasing the player character's flat damage absorption. Notable among these indirect bonuses is a reduction to fall-damage with every level invested into Dexterity.

title: Great Hammers (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Great Hammers (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Great Hammers** are a type of weapon in *Dark Souls III*.

The largest and most powerful class of ultra weapon, great hammers possess the heftiest Poise health and inflict the most Poise damage of all ultra weapons, making them the strongest Hyper Armor weapons in the game. With the exception of the Pickaxe, all great hammers inflict Strike damage, which is the least-resisted physical damage type on the vast majority of all armor, allowing these weapons to inflict much more damage than their peers. Like greataxes, great hammers possess very powerful vertical swings that can stagger foes in an area around the impact point, which can interrupt enemies attempting to outspace the wielder's swings even if they take no damage.

title: Greataxes (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Greataxes (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Greataxes** are a type of weapon in *Dark Souls III*.

One of the three classes of ultra weapons, greataxes are characterized by their heavy weight, hefty stamina cost and slow swing speed, in exchange for providing strong Hyper Armor and high damage output. Like other ultra weapons, they benefit greatly from investing heavily in Endurance, Vitality and Strength.

Among all ultra weapons, greataxes have a mundane moveset and the least range, but make up for this by inflicting the most damage. As well, like great hammers their vertical swings can inflict stagger on foes in an area around the impact point, making this weapon difficult to space against even by skilled opponents. As the big brother to the axe weapon class, several greataxes also possess the Warcry skill, allowing them to amplify their already high damage output to extreme levels.

title: Greatshields (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Greatshields (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - shield - lead 
 lead : **Greatshields** are a type of shield in *Dark Souls III*.

Greatshields are characterized by their immense weight, high Strength requirement, and extremely strong defenses. Because of their high weight, most greatshields will require the wielder to invest not only in Strength, but also Vitality, as well as Endurance to fortify their stamina pool. However, properly wielded, a greatshield will easily protect the player from most forms of damage from all but the strongest of foes. Greatshields are incapable of performing parries, and instead allow the wielder to Shield Bash their foes, or perform the Weapon Skill of their right-hand weapon without having to two-hand it.

Because of their innately high stability, upgrading a greatshield is crucial, as increasing their already strong stability will allow them to virtually ignore the stamina damage dealt by smaller weapons.

title: Hammers (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Hammers (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Hammers** are a weapon type in *Dark Souls III*.

Hammers are generally blunt weapons which inflict strike and/or thrust damage, depending on the specific weapon. They are the smallest-sized weapons which have Hyper Armor frames, allowing them to take advantage of Poise, though they are generally only effective at trading against similarly sized weapons. Offensively, they have moderate swing speed and crushing overhead strikes which are powerful for dealing with single targets, and they can deal Poise damage rivaling that of Greatswords. Most Hammers, with the exception of the Drang Hammers, have relatively low Dexterity requirements, making them ideal for Strength builds.

snippet:
Refined Gem -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Can be used to create Refined weapons through Blacksmith Andre in Firelink Shrine.

Infusing a weapon with a Refined Gem will increase the scaling bonuses from both Strength and Dexterity, without compromising one or the other, while also equalizing their scaling. While it does also lower the weapon's base damage slightly, the improved scaling bonuses, in most cases, will result in an overall damage increase.

Refined infusions are a solid choice if a player is utilizing a quality build, where Strength and Dexterity are leveled equally. Furthermore, Refined weapons are still able to be fully buffed by resins, bundles, or spells.

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - notes 
 notes : At around 45 Intelligence and onward, the Moonlight Greatsword should be infused with a Faintstone, as the higher scaling bonus begins to overcome the base damage drop.
When infused with a Magic Stone, this weapon's pure Magic damage is replaced by pure Physical damage, and its physical damage reduction goes from 60% to 93.3%, making its block more efficient than most shields against physical attacks. However, this completely nullifies the damage caused by the greatsword's signature strong attack, but the poise damage remains intact.
Due to its relatively low Strength and Dexterity requirements, this weapon is a perfect fit for pure mage builds.

title: Moonlight Butterfly Horn
snippet:
Moonlight Butterfly Horn -  Dark Souls - weapon - description 
 description : Weapon born from the mystical creature of Darkroot Garden, the Moonlight Butterfly.

The horns of the butterfly, a being created by Seath, are imbued with a pure magic power.

title: Barbed Straight Sword
snippet:
Barbed Straight Sword -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Despite what the description stating that Barbed Straight Sword deals thrust attacks, its moveset mostly features regular swing attacks, making it troublesome to use in close quarters.

Though considered a "Quality Scaling" weapon, Barbed Straight Sword is not on par with with other weapons in the Straight Sword class due to its lower base damage and its low 31% Strength and 50% Dexterity scaling. Though it deals Bleed build-up at a rate of 33 per strike, this sword is not worth it overall.

title: Pontiff Knight Curved Sword
snippet:
Pontiff Knight Curved Sword -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Pontiff Knight Curved Sword is considered one of the best weapons in its class. Despite its heavy weight and long reach, it actually utilizes the "light curved sword" moveset of the Scimitar. This means that it is the longest reaching curved sword that can execute somersaulting slashes and flips, and thus possesses the speed and range to be a particularly deadly threat in PvP. The cost, however, is that its attacks use up more stamina than normal, requiring its wielder to refrain from executing too many consecutive attacks.

Because it does not upgrade with regular Titanite, it cannot be buffed or infused, and thus caters more towards a quality build than a pure Dexterity-focused one. Furthermore, the non-scaling Intelligence requirement for wielding the weapon further complicates its ease of use, though this is made up for by its skill.

title: Royal Greatsword
snippet:
Much like the Flamberge, the Royal Greatsword causes Bleed build-up. It provides a good amount of damage while being lighter and slightly more durable than most other greatswords.

Compared to the Flamberge, it is lighter and more durable, as well as being obtainable earlier, outside of , where either one can be found early on. However, it demands slightly higher stats and the blade is much shorter than the Flamberge, which impacts its usefulness somewhat, especially when multiple foes are faced at once. Additionally, the Flamberge is likely to have more bleed build-up per hit due to bleed scaling off of the player's Dexterity. Furthermore, despite the Flamberge's lower base damage, it is likely to deal more damage on an optimized build, as it gains an S scaling in Dexterity when fully upgraded, while the Royal Greatsword only reaches a B scaling in Strength.

title: Pike
snippet:
Despite what the item description says, the Pike does not have the longest range of non-projectile weapons. The Silver Knight Spear, Dragonslayer Spear, Moonlight Butterfly Horn, and Demon's Spear are all longer.

The Pike has the highest damage potential out of all spears with a quality build. It outperforms the other physical damage spears due to higher base damage or Strength scaling, and lacks the split damage of the spears that have higher AR. (Split damage is penalized against enemy armor, which lowers the performance of weapons that deal more than one damage type, despite their high AR.)

title: Drakeblood Greatsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet: Overall, the Drakeblood Greatsword possesses many intrinsic advantages that makes it very strong in the hands of a build that does not prioritize physical damage. Its innate elemental damage, combined with its ability to be buffed or infused, make it a force to be reckoned with when buffed with Lightning Blade, Darkmoon Blade or Crystal Magic Weapon, or when infused with any number of elemental gems to amplify its damage output.

title: Pate's Spear
snippet:
Pate's Spear -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Pate's Spear is the second-strongest spear for a quality or Dexterity build. It is only bested by Yorgh's Spear. However, Yorgh's Spear performs much more like a Lance than a Spear. Thus, Pate's Spear is the strongest actual spear for these builds.

It performs much like an improved version of the Pike. However, it is upgraded with Twinkling Titanite, which may be unattractive to some players.

title: Profaned Greatsword
snippet:
Profaned Greatsword -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : A true quality weapon, the Profaned Greatsword is a well-balanced ultra greatsword with a versatile moveset and devastating power attacks.

While it tends slightly towards Strength in its scaling, the Profaned Greatsword also scales very well with Dexterity, granting it formidable damage output on builds that focus on leveling physical stats. It is also one of the lightest weapons in its class, only outweighing the Astora Greatsword and Zweihander of the ultra greatswords that can be two-handed. It also has the third-highest base damage of the ultra greatswords, after the Black Knight Greatsword and the Ringed Knight Paired Greatswords, and on a full quality build is out-damaged only by the Black Knight Greatsword when two-handed.

title: Poison Gem
snippet:
Poison Gem -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Infuses a weapon with Poison, allowing it to inflict the Poison status effect and increasing in effectiveness with the wielder's Luck. Weapons that innately inflict Poison build-up are granted increased build-up and improved Luck scaling.

Greatly reduces Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence and Faith scaling, as well as base damage.

title: Herald (class)
snippet:
Herald (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Herald** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a hybrid class, with a decent amount of Vigor, Strength, Dexterity, and Faith, but a slightly below average Attunement (especially for a class with a starting spell) and Endurance. It seems intended to provide the basis for a build more focused on either one of Strength or Dexterity or a mix of both, that still has the stats to carry some supportive Miracles from its Faith.

Its Spear deals somewhat mediocre damage and is quite short for a polearm, but is actually fairly quick and can attack while still keeping a block up, at the cost of lowering that block's effectiveness (meaning even a 100% block shield will let some damage slip through if hit). Its skill is Shield Splitter, a heavy thrust that partially bypasses blocking.

title: Painting Guardian's Curved Sword
snippet:
Painting Guardian's Curved Sword -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Painting Guardian's Curved Sword is a low-weight curved sword (the second-lightest in its class, beat only by the Demon's Scar) that uses the "light curved sword" moveset of the Scimitar and requires little stamina to swing. However, it has a reach more akin to that of a dagger than a curved sword. It also possesses high dexterity scaling, despite being a standard Titanite weapon, as well as a respectable amount of Bleed build-up.

What makes the Painting Guardian's Curved Sword unique is its weapon art. Unlike the Spin Slash of other curved swords, the Chained Dance unleashes a combo of several strong slashes with the strong attack, which can be devastating on exposed foes due to the Bleed build-up.

title: Sorcerer (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Sorcerer (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Sorcerer** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It is an Intelligence-based class, serving as an excellent base for a build focused on Sorceries or Hexes, and also possibly for a build using a Magic infused weapon that wants to start with some spells. It has a decent starting Dexterity but a horrendous starting Strength, barely even enough to wield their weapon and even with effective Strength being doubled when two-handing so the vast majority of weapons can't be wielded without some investment, only some Daggers.

The starting Sorcerer's Staff is a decent, quick-casting spell tool for Sorceries that is worth upgrading, while the Dagger is a decent, if short reaching weapon whose poor Durability should be supplemented by picking up a second copy in the Things Betwixt tutorial.

title: Paired Weapons
snippet:
Paired Weapons -  Dark Souls III - weapon - notes 
 notes : Though it is not a paired weapon in the same way as the others and can be two-handed normally, Friede's Great Scythe behaves similarly to a paired weapon when its skill is active.
The player's Strength is not boosted when two-handing a paired weapon.
Status effect build-up is reduced on each individual hit when using a paired weapon's L1/LB attack. Due to the multi-hit nature of this attack, this means that it will still inflict more build-up if both attacks connect.
** This reduction only applies to a weapon's innate status build-up. As such, Carthus Rouge and Rotten Pine Resin will still cause their full amount of build-up per hit regardless of what attack is used. This makes weapons like the Crow Talons and Warden Twinblades extremely dangerous when buffed with Carthus Rouge.

title: Follower Sabre
snippet:
Follower Sabre -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : On initial inspection, the Follower Sabre is not a very impressive weapon, as it uses the standard "heavy curved sword" moveset of the Falchion.

However, what distinguishes the Follower Sabre, besides its longer reach, is its weapon art, the Prying Wedge. This gives the Follower Sabre a niche where its brethren often have trouble, performing lightning-fast guard breaks. This serves to greatly augment its offensive potential, rewarding aggressive players who are able to put constant pressure on their foes.

Unusual for a curved sword, it can reach A scaling in Strength when upgraded and infused with Heavy. A quality build with Refined will still have a higher attack rating, however.

title: Poison (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Poison (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - boosting_poison_build_up 
 boosting_poison_build_up : There are two pieces of equipment that can grant a flat bonus to the Poison buildup stat on Poison weapons when worn. The bonus granted from these items can vary depending on what type of Poison weapon is equipped, be it innate Poison, infused Poison or both. Both of these items can be worn together, which would provide double the bonus.

The following numbers are the menu numbers but they are applied as a fifth of that on hit.

title: Yhorm's Great Machete
snippet: However, because it is a soul-transposed weapon and highly specialized towards Strength builds, this means that it is incapable of being easily wielded by anything short of Strength-heavy or quality builds. As well, being a machete-type weapon, its two-handed weak attacks are incapable of staggering foes long enough for two-hit combos, short of situations involving elevation disparities between the wielder and target. This means that in order to be wielded optimally, Yhorm's Great Machete is best held in only one hand, further requiring a specialized build to make use of it.

title: Swordsman
snippet:
Swordsman -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Swordsman** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It has the highest Dexterity of the starting classes, making it a good base for a build focused on that stat, such as one using Curved Swords and Bows. Additionally, a decent base Attunement and Intelligence makes using support Sorceries such as Magic Weapon easier.

The starting weapons this class wields are the only ones that are upgraded (though only to +1) and are compatible with each other for the purpose of Power Stancing, though another 2 points in Strength and 8 points in Dexterity are needed for that. Instead, it may be easier to either focus on one of the weapons as the main weapon, with perhaps a shield from Maughlin the Armorer in the other hand, or to get a second Shortsword from the Forest of Fallen Giants as that only requires the 2 extra points in Strength to begin Power Stancing.

title: Club (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Like some other weapons, the Club can be used to trivialize major parts of the game, due to its ability to stunlock most regular enemies with its one-handed weak attack. For this reason, a Strength build (or any build, with enough patience), can comfortably use the club throughout the entire game (including on NG+ and onward).

Its high damage relative to its weight makes the Club a good candidate for use with Flynn's Ring.

title: Friede's Great Scythe
snippet: These advantages do not come without drawbacks, however. In order to wield the weapon, players must first invest a non-negligible amount of levels in Faith, which makes the weapon more difficult to build for. Additionally, despite what is listed in the weapon's information, with its normal moveset it cannot inflict Magic damage at all. As such, in regular situations this reaper is little different from the Pontiff Knight Great Scythe.

title: Crest of Blood
snippet:
Crest of Blood -  Dark Souls II - ring - effect 
 effect : The Crest of Blood boosts a weapon's Bleed attack by 50 points. However, this only affects weapons that deal Bleed build-up, and the ring is thus useless unless the weapon has either innate Bleed build-up, or if it's been infused with a Bleed Stone.

title: Black Blade
snippet:
Black Blade -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Black Blade is a katana with some simple trade-offs that lets it stand out as a unique weapon within its class. Its primary draw is its high damage, a Sharp-infused Black Blade being one of the highest damage katanas available for a Dexterity-focused build, but it is somewhat short and heavy, and has a hefty strength requirement of 18 that may make it inaccessible for some builds.

title: Carthus Rouge
snippet:
Carthus Rouge -  Dark Souls III - item - effect 
 effect : Adds 20 Bleed build-up to right-hand weapon for 60 seconds. A Blood Loss proc will inflict an additional 100 damage if the threshold was crossed by the build-up from a Carthus Rouge buffed weapon.

The build-up increase scales with the Luck of the wielder, increasing up to to 26 build-up at 50 Luck.

title: Shortsword
snippet:
Shortsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Shortsword has the exact same "Quality" scaling as a majority of the other Straight Swords, though with less base damage to scale from. The Quality scaling of this sword makes it a bit inefficient to use from a stat perspective, though it will be its best at the softcaps for Strength and Dexterity. Its main early advantage is a quick and efficient thrust R2 attack, and its short range makes it useful in hallways and at corners.

title: Herald Armor
snippet:
Herald Armor -  Dark Souls III - armor - description 
 description : Steel armor with a pure white cape, the signature of Heralds of the way of White.

Protection made of steel has excellent physical absorption, but is found lacking against blunt strikes and lightning damage.

title: Herald Set
snippet:
Herald Set -  Dark Souls III - armor - description 
 description : Steel armor with a pure white cape, the signature of Heralds of the Way of White.

Protection made of steel has excellent physical absorption, but is found lacking against blunt strikes and lightning damage.

title: Deprived
snippet:
Deprived -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Deprived** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls*.

With absolutely no armor and all stats at 11, the Deprived will force the beginning player to scavenge for, or purchase, a decent armor and shield. This class' lack of any usable gear is evened out by the aforementioned equal stats; allowing for excellent build variety. It can be good for new players who want to challenge themselves, but otherwise offers no advantages over a more specialized starting class.

title: Ledo's Great Hammer
snippet:
However, when players do not activate the smash attack, the weapon will remain buffed by the stone that wraps it, giving it significantly more damage for some time before disappearing. The player can break the stones around the weapon and deal the area-of-effect blast anytime within the duration by performing a charged strong attack, making it a very versatile skill that can be used strategically.

The weapon gains a superb A scaling in Strength with enough upgrades and has no other stat requirements, making it most effective on pure strength builds.

title: Sun Sword
snippet:
Sun Sword -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Sun Sword possesses amazing scaling across strength and dexterity. This makes it an exceptional choice for quality builds and allows the weapon to perform admirably even at base level, assuming the player can use the stat scaling to the fullest. This means that the sword will outdamage other straight swords with a dedicated quality build.

However, the weapon falters if the player has low strength and dexterity. It also synergizes poorly with infusions, as the weapon's physical scaling is drastically reduced while its elemental scaling is similar to the average straight sword, and its base damage remains low.

Consumable weapon buffs such as Gold Pine Resin and Rotten Pine Resin make excellent complements for this weapon. Spells such as Sunlight Blade, Crystal Magic Weapon, and Sacred Oath, can also be used to offset its otherwise poor synergy with quality/faith and quality/intelligence builds.

title: Gargoyle Flame Hammer
snippet:
Gargoyle Flame Hammer -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Scales best with Strength but the fairly high base fire damage means it works fairly well on a pyromancer (Intelligence/Faith) build with only moderate amounts of Strength.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Gwyn's title uses the kanji "薪の王" that can be literally translated as "King of Kindling" or "King of Firewood".
Gwyn's design and lore seems to have been heavily inspired by Zeus of ancient Greek mythology.
Several aspects of him can also be compared to the Welsh deity Gwyn ap Nudd.
**Gwyn ap Nudd is said to be a warrior with a "blackened face" similar to Gwyn's hollowed flesh, and the King of the "fair folk." The gods of Lordran being a fair folk.
**In Arthurian legends and writings, Gwyn ap Nudd was the ruler of a delightful paradise called the otherworld, or Annwn. Such a place would be similar to Anor Londo during its glory days.
**Additionally, one can make a comparison between Gwyn ap Nudd leading the Wild Hunt in Welsh legend, and the dragon hunts of Gwyn.
"Gwyn" translated from Welsh means "White/Pure" or "Holy".

title: Caestus (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Caestus (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Caestus is one of only two fist weapons in the game, the other being the Bone Fist. The Caestus does not replace the player's hand armor, but goes over the top of it, and cannot be wielded in the same slot as another weapon. In terms of scaling, the Caestus is one of the best weapons in the game for a build with somewhat-balanced Strength and Dexterity stats, as at full-reinforcement, the Dexterity scaling improves, going from B to A.

When two Caestuses are power-stanced, they are capable of stunning enemies with the weak power-stanced attack (LB/L1), allowing for multiple hits that can quickly rack up damage.

title: Berserker Blade
snippet:
Berserker Blade -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Bersker Blade is one of the highest damage katanas available, and it features a standard moveset revolving around vertical slashes and delayed strong attacks. Its main drawbacks compared to other katanas are its short length, and the time-consuming way it is obtained.

Being a rare drop from the Mad Warrior and Prowlers; the process of even getting this weapon can be arduous, but its excellent scaling in dexterity allows it to compete with the Chaos Blade. Compared to the Chaos Blade, it also comes with the advantages of not draining the wielder's health points and being more easily accessible, though likely slower to obtain, due to the nature of random drops.

title: Bleed (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Bleed (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - item - build_up 
 build_up : When the Bleed effect occurs a build-up bar will appear in the middle of the screen. Blood Loss will take effect when the bleed meter fills up. The size of the bar is determined by the amount of resistance to bleed the player has.

title: Blacksteel Katana
snippet:
Blacksteel Katana -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Blacksteel Katana's initial strong attacks (1-handed and 2-handed) are very similar to the Iaito from *Dark Souls, *which are then followed up with a thrusting attack. It is also able to chain together its 2-handed weak attacks into strong attacks, which can chain into yet another strong attack, stunning most low-Poise enemies and racking up damage quickly.

This is a very potent weapon, much like the Chaos Blade, for pure-Dexterity builds, as it scales purely with Dexterity unless it is infused with elemental damage. It should be noted that after a few upgrades are pumped into it, the Dexterity scaling bonus changes from A to S.

title: Dancer's Enchanted Swords
snippet:
Dancer's Enchanted Swords -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Dancer's Enchanted Swords are a rather unique set of curved swords, even among paired weapons. Utilizing the heavy curved sword moveset of the Falchion, the Dancer's Swords will inflict physical damage as well as either Magic or Fire damage, depending on the blade that connects.

The scaling on these weapons is also very peculiar. Leveling Strength and Dexterity will not only increase the physical damage of the blades, but will also increase both the Magic and Fire damage. Leveling Intelligence will increase both the Magic and Fire damage, while leveling Faith will increase only the Fire damage. This means that the most efficient way to increase damage output on these weapons is on a quality build, and that the Fire damage of the off-hand sword will be increased no matter which stat is leveled.

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - soft_caps 
 soft_caps : In terms of "return on investment" (for strength and scaling), unlike in *Dark Souls*, players get the "best" return on investment in the 30~40 range. The gains go something like this:
0~30 : 100%
30~40 : 150%
40~50 : 50%
50~60 : 25%
Where "100%" represents an arbitrary scale of what the player would get per point for a given rating.

In terms of scaling, it means the best gains are for "putting all your eggs in the same basket", with either "40/20" for Strength/quality or "20/40" for Dexterity, but never "30/30".

title: Sunlight Straight Sword
snippet:
Sunlight Straight Sword -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Sunlight Straight Sword has the exact same "Quality" scaling as a majority of other Straight Swords. This weapon has identical base damage and scaling compared with Broadsword and Dark Sword. Sunlight Straight Sword shares its moveset with Longsword, though it has better base damage, higher durability, higher requirements, is one unit heavier, and has slightly slower attacks.

While slightly better than the Longsword, the Sunlight Straight Sword still pales in comparison to the Uchigatana or Iaito, which are both longer, and get close to or exceed its 40/40 Strength/Dexterity damage output at only 14 Strength. This allows the player to devote levels into Intelligence or Faith for Weapon Buffs. It is therefore not a recommended weapon to use in general combat.

title: Dragonslayer Greatbow (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Dragonslayer Greatbow (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Dragonslayer Greatbow, at first, seems to be unremarkable for its weight and lower base damage, when compared to the Alonne Greatbow. However, what makes the former outclass the latter greatbow is its improved Strength scaling, as well as requiring more Strength instead of Dexterity, effectively making the Dragonslayer Greatbow a Strength-oriented greatbow. This greatbow also consumes a very large amount of stamina per shot, meaning most players may only get one effective shot fired before low stamina penalties begin to occur on the successive attacks.

title: Londor
snippet: as well as lethal curved claws that caused heavy bleeding. They donned pure white attire and golden masks with faint, kindly smiles which earned them the moniker "Harlots of Death". Sir Vilhelm, a knight of Londor known as a cold-blooded hangman, would also report directly to the three sisters of the Sable Church, becoming particularly loyal to Elfriede.

title: Ledo's Great Hammer
snippet:
The weapon gains a superb A scaling in Strength with enough upgrades and has no other stat requirements, making it most effective on pure strength builds.

Ledo's Great Hammer also has very obvious drawbacks. It is the heaviest weapon in the game at 28 units. Although its attacks grant large amounts of poise, they are slow and predictable. In addition, its massive size can obstruct the players view of their surroundings, much like (but not to the extent of) Smough's Great Hammer. It also consumes more stamina per attack than a regular great hammer, such as the Great Mace. Players without high investment in Endurance may find it necessary to equip stamina-boosting items, such as the Chloranthy Ring, or use Green Blossoms to use this weapon effectively.
